coverage_note: This register holds requirement-level assertion evidence. The exhaustive v1.19 requirement inventory (every endpoint, module, room version component and appendix section with status, code, tests and gap beads) is docs/spec-inventory.json (human view: docs/spec-inventory.md). Passing tests cover only the assertions named. Endpoint presence does not establish semantic conformance.

assertions: Content hashes cover unredacted typed-event content
Reference hashes redact then omit signatures and unsigned
Local event_id is excluded from hashes and signatures
Ed25519 bytes match an independent OpenSSL vector
limitations: Unknown PDU fields are not retained; no separate PDU wire model

assertions: Known event types retain the v11 content subset
Create content is retained
Only third_party_invite.signed survives member pruning
Unsigned data is removed
limitations: Top-level unknown fields and other room-version rules still need a wire-model audit

assertions: v2 send_join and invite resolve at standard paths
Missing authentication is rejected
Authentication covers the full URI through nesting
Former incorrectly versioned paths are absent
limitations: This does not prove complete join/invite authorization, PDU shape, or independent peer interoperability

assertions: Device-list positions do not skip queued messages
Messages persist until a following sync acknowledges their cursor
Repeated sync and process restart preserve unacknowledged messages
Acknowledging an earlier batch retains later messages
Wildcard targets expand to actual devices
Acknowledgement by one device preserves other device queues
Pending and newly queued messages complete long-polls promptly
limitations: Full federation surfaces and commit-order/snapshot consistency remain open

assertions: Normal UIA registration and password login work through the binary
Profile and message Unicode survives HTTP/storage
Two users create/join/send/sync
Retry before restart returns the same event
Restart preserves tokens, signing keys and message history
Logout invalidates the device token
limitations: These journeys do not establish complete client-server conformance or durable transaction deduplication

assertions: Port zero reports actual bound address after migrations
Malformed/occupied addresses and unwritable readiness files fail startup
Fixture owns and cleans up isolated process/database/media

scope: Canonical JSON and PDU validation/authorization/state resolution
assertions: Every v1.19 endpoint (client-server 164 incl. 9 deprecated, server-server 36, application-service 11, push-gateway 1, identity-service 23) is enumerated from the published HTML and cross-checked against each page's endpoint TOC
Every homeserver-relevant module/section, room versions 1-12 (5 components each) and every appendix section is enumerated
Each item records status, code location, test location and gap beads; every partial/missing/untested item names a bead; every not-applicable item states its justification
limitations: Inventory snapshot of main at 8e301e5 (after conduit-y99.18 account/devices and conduit-y99.19 room content landed); lanes conduit-y99.13/.14/.15/.16/.22/.23 and conduit-embed-pdu change rows as they land and must update docs/spec-inventory.json
Status implemented+tested means named tests assert the behaviour, not that every clause is proven; full_compliance_proven remains false
Olm/Megolm client interactions are client-side and tracked by conduit-y99.9, not by homeserver rows

evidence: client/ is a TypeScript/React web client with its own framework-free CS-API core (client/src/core) and an accessible UI (client/src/ui)
Unit: cd client && pnpm test (Vitest: core HTTP/auth/discovery/sync/room/send-queue, UI logic, WCAG token contrast)
E2E: cd client && pnpm e2e (Playwright against the real conduit-server binary and a fresh PostgreSQL database)
scope: Unattended unit, integration and browser e2e verification
limitations: Phase 1 only: no media, typing/receipt/presence UI, relations, device management, room settings, directory or E2EE yet (child beads of conduit-y99.9)
E2E runs Chromium only
Unread counts fall back to client-side counting while the server sends zeros (conduit-y99.24)

assertions: Matrix error bodies parse into errcode, message and HTTP status; non-JSON errors get a synthetic errcode
429 waits for Retry-After (seconds) in preference to retry_after_ms, then retries
5xx and connection failures back off exponentially and give up after the retry budget
4xx errors are not retried; M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN (incl. soft_logout) is reported to the session owner
Full URLs are validated through /_matrix/client/versions
Server names and Matrix IDs use .well-known/matrix/client m.homeserver.base_url
404 well-known is IGNOREd (falls back to https://server_name); malformed well-known is FAIL_PROMPT; a non-homeserver is FAIL_ERROR
tests: client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::an unreachable homeserver is reported on the homeserver field

assertions: Password login uses an m.id.user identifier and honours a login well_known override
Registration completes UIA m.login.dummy with the server's session and fails clearly on unsupported stages
Logout revokes the token on the server (whoami afterwards returns M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN) and wipes local state
tests: client/e2e/chat.spec.ts::a session survives reload and sign-out revokes it
client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::sign-in validates input and explains server errors

assertions: Initial sync with timeout=0, then long-poll with the persisted since token and a stable inline filter
Room state is folded from state then timeline; limited timelines reset the window to prev_batch
Invites come from invite_state; rooms in leave are removed
Failures move to reconnecting with backoff, recover on retry, and M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN stops the session
since token and room snapshots persist across reloads
tests: client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::losing the sync connection shows a reconnecting banner and recovers
client/e2e/chat.spec.ts::a session survives reload and sign-out revokes it

assertions: Room names use m.room.name, then m.room.canonical_alias, then heroes (summary or members), then Empty room (was ...)
Invites are named from stripped state or the inviter
Clashing member display names are disambiguated with the user ID
Each message keeps one transaction ID across retries, failures and restarts
Local echoes reconcile by event ID, including when the remote echo arrives before the PUT response
Failed sends show inline retry and delete; retry delivers exactly once
tests: client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::a failed send shows inline retry and delete, and retry delivers once
client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::failed sends survive a reload and can be retried afterwards
limitations: Reconciliation by unsigned.transaction_id is implemented but untested against Conduit, which omits it (conduit-y99.27)

assertions: Back-pagination starts from the sync prev_batch, prepends oldest-first without changing current state and de-duplicates
An absent/empty end or empty chunk marks the start of the room
75 seeded messages page back to the beginning exactly once and in order
tests: client/e2e/resilience.spec.ts::scrolling back pages history until the start of the room

assertions: Create (public/private, name, topic), invite, accept, decline, join by room ID and leave work end to end between two browser sessions
tests: client/e2e/chat.spec.ts::two people create a room, invite, accept and chat both ways
client/e2e/chat.spec.ts::join by room ID, validate addresses, and leave

assertions: axe reports zero serious or critical WCAG 2.x A/AA violations on sign-in, home, room, failed send, dialogs and settings in light and dark
Every design-token text pair meets 4.5:1 and indicators 3:1 in both themes
Room list and timeline are arrow-key navigable; focus moves on route changes; incoming messages are announced
limitations: Automated checks only; no manual screen-reader audit yet

evidence: Pinned live Synapse 1.162.0 bidirectional to-device journey passes with certificate, hostname and signature verification enabled
limitations: CI and full independent protocol coverage remain missing

assertions: Subscribe before observing pending streams
Non-room wake hints do not trigger push/AS room-event workers
To-device, device-list, account-data, receipt, typing and presence updates end a long-poll
Typing stop and expiry emit empty replacement lists
Restart resets ephemeral cursors without resetting durable cursors
Account-data and receipt overwrites use real observed stream positions
Room-only account data and ephemeral updates appear without new timeline events
Unchanged visible data waits until the original deadline
limitations: Complete membership/state/full_state/filter/pagination semantics remain open
Commit-order and concurrent snapshot consistency need an independent audit
Durable changes from other processes currently use periodic polling

assertions: Private receipts are returned only to their owner
Multiple public receipt users coexist for the same event
Presence sync is restricted to self and shared joined-room users
Presence status reads require authentication and enforce visibility
Unrelated presence updates do not expose status or finish a poll early
limitations: Threaded and fully-read receipts and complete room/event authorization remain open
Federated presence is still missing

assertions: Sync reports own-device OTK counts and unused fallback algorithms
Pending upload and claim changes bypass the long-poll timeout
Fallback usage advances the inventory summary independently of device-list changes
Unchanged inventory does not cause busy polling
Inventory fingerprint uses canonical JSON
limitations: Independent encrypted clients (vodozemac/libolm) are not yet exercised end to end

assertions: Successful room-send results persist atomically with events
To-device deduplication, local queues and remote outboxes commit atomically
Concurrent retries have one committed effect
Scope includes user, device and complete logical endpoint
Retries survive restart and do not reexpand wildcard recipients
Failed writes roll back deduplication and all effects
Definitive rejected responses survive permission changes and restart
Completed responses replay before later body validation
Authentication still rejects revoked credentials before cached reply
A new access token for the same device retains replay scope
Interrupted body reads remain retryable
limitations: Event authorization/state publication and stream commit ordering need their separate audits

assertions: Remote deliveries use m.direct_to_device EDUs in standard /send transactions
Sender is the authenticated Matrix user, not a bare server name
Stable message IDs use at most 32 Unicode codepoints
Inbound sender domain matches the verified origin
Message-ID deduplication survives different enclosing transactions and restart
Queued remote delivery recovers after an unavailable peer and restart
Pinned live Synapse produces and consumes both directions over verified TLS
Whole enclosing HTTP transactions pin the first authenticated body and final response
A partial batch resumes only its unfinished original messages after transient failure and restart
Required origin/timestamp/PDUs and 50-PDU/100-EDU limits are enforced
Transport permits >2 MB batches within the 16 MB signed-body limit
limitations: Legacy senderless queued rows cannot be converted into valid EDUs
Full federation PDU/room-version/auth/peer conformance remains unproven

assertions: Operator PEM roots preserve normal outbound TLS verification
Missing and invalid configured roots fail startup
Live-peer fixture provisions processes, databases and certificates without human interaction
Missing prerequisites and assertion failures exit nonzero
Replay identities serialize across PG storage instances
Cancellation releases request guards
Lifetime locks do not starve the data connection pool
The first request and completed result remain immutable
HTTP status/parsing stay in the host, outside the pure kernel storage API
Transient failures retry the original request rather than freezing an error
limitations: Independent peer coverage here is limited to the named transaction/EDU assertions; complete protocol coverage remains open

assertions: Both claims queries and authorization use a bounded 50ms wall-clock evaluation budget
Default generated-fact and iteration bounds remain in force
Valid tokens verify under parallel load
Expiry, epoch, trust and attenuation rejection tests remain green
Oversized rule-generated fact sets fail closed
limitations: These tests cover the current capability backend; they do not prove every Matrix login/session flow

assertions: Memory event order uses actual insertion positions independently of DAG depth
Duplicate IDs retain the original event and do not advance cursors
Atomic event writes use the same stream
Membership history and pagination use actual event positions
Both backends retain a monotonic global cursor after purging the latest room
limitations: Out-of-order PostgreSQL commit/snapshot consistency remains under its own audit

assertions: Invite previews contain own membership and safe stripped room metadata
Acceptance introduces joined-room state
Kick/leave timelines include own transition and exclude later messages
Limited gaps carry state changes before the returned timeline
full_state returns immediately; filter limits must be strictly positive
prev_batch fetches omitted events without repeating the timeline boundary
limitations: Full DAG historical snapshots remain required
Remaining filter/format edges and knock API journeys remain incomplete

assertions: A standard Synapse-signed v11 create PDU without event_id must deserialize and persist its extensions
evidence: Current server returns PDU parse error: missing field event_id
Prepared add-pdu-wire change awaits independent review; configured Opus authentication expired and Grok fallback timed out

assertions: Filter creation/read are scoped to the authenticated owner
Definitions survive restart and inline/stored criteria agree
Wildcard type patterns, sender inclusion and exclusions, URL predicates and escaped field paths are supported
Empty lists select none; exclusions win; malformed and nonpositive limits reject
Lazy membership state includes self/timeline senders and omits unrelated members
Limited account-data/presence windows deliver remainder on following sync
Lazy membership lookup uses the snapshot before the timeline, not later profile updates
limitations: Raw federation event format is still the legacy snapshot pending PDU wire work
Broader state/ephemeral limit and lazy member edge auditing remains required

assertions: GET /publicRooms needs no auth; POST requires an access token (401 M_MISSING_TOKEN)
Chunks carry room_id, name, topic (plain text), canonical_alias, num_joined_members, world_readable, guest_can_join, avatar_url, join_rule, room_type
Stable order: largest joined count first, then room ID; total_room_count_estimate is the filtered count
limit/since paginate with next_batch and prev_batch; malformed since is 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
filter.generic_search_term matches name/topic/aliases case-insensitively; filter.room_types honours null for untyped rooms
include_all_networks and third_party_instance_id select application-service network lists; combining them is 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
createRoom visibility=public publishes; GET /directory/list/room reports public/private; unknown room 404 M_NOT_FOUND

PUT /directory/list/room requires a server admin or a joined member able to send m.room.canonical_alias (403 M_FORBIDDEN otherwise); visibility defaults to public; invalid visibility 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
PUT /directory/list/appservice/{networkId}/{roomId} is as_token-authenticated
limitations: server=<remote> proxies the federation GET /publicRooms and filters that page locally; not exercised against a live peer

assertions: PUT/GET/DELETE /directory/room/{alias}; existing alias 409 M_UNKNOWN; malformed or foreign alias 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
GET resolves to room_id and servers; missing alias 404 M_NOT_FOUND
DELETE allowed for the creator, a server admin or a member able to set m.room.canonical_alias; otherwise 403; missing 404
GET /rooms/{roomId}/aliases is for joined members or world_readable rooms (403 M_FORBIDDEN)
POST /join/{roomIdOrAlias} resolves local aliases; unknown alias 404 M_NOT_FOUND
createRoom room_alias_name binds the alias, sets m.room.canonical_alias, and rejects a taken alias with 400 M_ROOM_IN_USE
limitations: Remote aliases resolve via federation query/directory but join of remote rooms is not implemented

assertions: Searches users sharing a room with the requester and users joined to public-join-rule or world_readable rooms; others are invisible
Case-insensitive match on user ID and display name; display_name/avatar_url from the profile
limit defaults to 10; limited reports truncation; shared-room users rank first
Missing search_term 400 M_MISSING_PARAM; wrong type 400 M_BAD_JSON; unauthenticated 401
limitations: Remote user directories are not queried (SHOULD)

assertions: POST /knock/{roomIdOrAlias} by room ID or alias returns room_id and records reason
Only knock/knock_restricted rooms accept knocks; banned, invited or joined users are refused 403 M_FORBIDDEN; unknown room or alias 404
Knock auth events include m.room.join_rules (auth events selection)
rooms.knock in /sync carries stripped knock_state (create, name, topic, join_rules, own member) without event IDs
Knocker cannot join directly; invite accepts (rooms.invite then join); kick denies; self-leave rescinds (rooms.leave)
v11 leave rules: self-leave from knock; kick governs any non-ban target; unban also needs the ban level
limitations: Knocking on rooms this server is not in (make_knock/send_knock over federation) is not implemented

assertions: GET /thirdparty/protocols aggregates registered application services' protocols; {} with none
Protocol instances gain instance_id {appservice_id}|{network_id}, usable as third_party_instance_id
protocol/location/user lookups proxy the AS API with Bearer hs_token and pass the client's fields through; nothing found is 404 M_NOT_FOUND
location?alias and user?userid route to ASes whose namespaces match; missing parameter 400 M_MISSING_PARAM
Requires the path appservice's own as_token (403 M_FORBIDDEN for other AS or user tokens; 401 without token)
Calls POST /_matrix/app/v1/ping with Bearer hs_token and the transaction_id; returns duration_ms
url: null is 400 M_URL_NOT_SET; non-2xx is 502 M_BAD_STATUS with status and body; refused connection 502 M_CONNECTION_FAILED; >10s 504 M_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT
Content-Type is returned exactly as uploaded; absent upload type is application/octet-stream
Content-Disposition is inline only for the spec's inline-safe list, attachment otherwise
Upload filename (query parameter) or path override is reproduced exactly, RFC 8187 for non-ASCII, omitted when absent
Recommended Content-Security-Policy, nosniff and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy are sent
Invalid media IDs are 404 and invalid server names 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
Authenticated download/upload reject missing tokens
limitations: Downloads are never redirected (allowed by the spec)

assertions: Media stored after the freeze is 404 M_NOT_FOUND on deprecated download/thumbnail endpoints
Media stored before the freeze remains reachable unauthenticated
Remote cache fills count as new media; deprecated endpoints never fetch remote media
allow_redirect=true still returns the content
The freeze can be disabled by the operator
limitations: No m.login.sso IdP icon exemption (no IdP icons are served)

assertions: v1 and v3 config return the same m.upload.size and require authentication
Uploads above the configured limit are 413 M_TOO_LARGE; uploads above 2 MiB but within the limit succeed
Oversized remote media is 502 M_TOO_LARGE
Remote media is 404 M_NOT_FOUND without fetching when federation is disabled
limitations: No per-user upload quota

assertions: create returns content_uri and unused_expires_at (24h default)
Pending media downloads wait up to timeout_ms then 504 M_NOT_YET_UPLOADED, and complete when content arrives
Only the creator may upload (403 M_FORBIDDEN); existing content is 409 M_CANNOT_OVERWRITE_MEDIA
Unknown, foreign or expired IDs are 404 M_NOT_FOUND
Too many pending uploads per user is 429 M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with retry_after_ms; expired reservations stop counting
width and height are required positive integers; method is crop or scale; animated is boolean
scale preserves aspect and is never smaller than requested; crop returns the requested size
Content is never upscaled; small content is returned as-is
Static output unless animated=true
Thumbnail Content-Disposition is inline
Non-images are 400 M_UNKNOWN; oversized images 413 M_TOO_LARGE
limitations: Animated thumbnails are only produced by passing through small animated originals

assertions: v1 and deprecated v3 preview_url require authentication
HTML OpenGraph og:* properties are returned with title/description fallbacks
og:image is re-hosted as an mxc URI with og:image:type, dimensions and matrix:image:size
Results are cached; ts selects the newest preview at or before ts, else a newer one
Loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, ULA, IPv4-mapped and NAT64-embedded destinations are refused before connecting, including after redirects and for og:image
Bodies over the size cap are 502 M_TOO_LARGE (with or without Content-Length); the fetch deadline is enforced
limitations: HTML is decoded as UTF-8 only; no oEmbed

assertions: Remote media is fetched from /_matrix/federation/v1/media/download, multipart/mixed parsed, cached and served without refetching
The remote Content-Disposition filename is reused
Remote 404 maps to M_NOT_FOUND
limitations: Inbound federation media endpoints answer raw bytes rather than multipart/mixed
Not yet verified against a live Synapse peer

assertions: GET /event serves the client event format (no PDU-only fields, unsigned.age) with bundled aggregations
Unknown events and events the user may not see are both 404 M_NOT_FOUND
GET /members filters membership/not_membership (or-combined), rejects unknown values with M_INVALID_PARAM, honours at tokens and returns 403 to never-members
Departed users see members and history as of their departure only
GET /context returns events_before reverse-chronologically and events_after chronologically, split from limit, with state at the last returned event
Context start/end tokens continue pagination through /messages; the RoomEventFilter applies to before/after/state with lazy member loading
GET /joined_rooms lists only rooms with join membership
limitations: Historical state is folded from stream order, not resolved DAG snapshots (see conduit-y99.13)

assertions: PUT /redact is idempotent per transaction ID through persisted transactions
Own events need the m.room.redaction level; other users' events need redact; server admins may redact local users' events
PUT /send of m.room.redaction obeys the same permission rules
Redacted events are pruned by the room-version algorithm and carry unsigned.redacted_because on /event, /messages, /sync and context
A redaction applies only from the same server or a sender with redact power in the redaction's own auth power levels
m.room.redaction events mirror content.redacts at top level for older clients
limitations: Original content remains in storage although never served

assertions: Forgetting while joined is 400 M_UNKNOWN
Forgotten rooms leave /sync (including include_leave) and their history becomes unreadable
Rejoining un-forgets; forgetting a room never joined is a no-op
POST /read_markers stores m.fully_read room account data and m.read / m.read.private receipts
Markers must name visible events of the room (404 M_NOT_FOUND otherwise)
Private receipts are visible only to their owner in /sync
Room tags are stored as m.tag room account data, appear in /sync, reject non-numeric order with M_BAD_JSON and are owner-only (403)
Deleting an absent tag succeeds
GET /v1/relations supports relType and eventType forms, dir, from/to, limit and prev_batch/next_batch pagination
recurse=true follows indirect relations to depth 3 and reports recursion_depth; it is absent unless recurse was supplied
Parents the user cannot see are 404 M_NOT_FOUND
Bundled m.replace is the latest valid edit (same sender/type, m.new_content, not state) and original content is not replaced
Redacting the latest edit reverts the bundle to the previous edit
Bundled m.thread reports count, latest_event and current_user_participated; m.reference lists referencing event IDs; annotations are not aggregated
GET /v1/threads orders roots by latest activity, paginates, supports include=participated and rejects invalid include
Duplicate annotations are rejected with M_DUPLICATE_ANNOTATION; threads off relations with 400 M_UNKNOWN
dir=f returns the earliest visible event at or after ts and dir=b the latest at or before it
No event is 404 M_NOT_FOUND; missing dir/ts is 400 M_INVALID_PARAM; non-members are 403
limitations: No federation fallback for rooms with incomplete local history

assertions: room_events searches content.body/name/topic with PostgreSQL full-text stemming and honours keys
Only events the user may see are searched, including left rooms up to the departure; redacted and ignored events are excluded
order_by rank|recent, filter limit with next_batch pagination and count
event_context returns events before/after with tokens and historic profile_info
include_state and room_id/sender groupings are returned
Missing search_term is M_BAD_JSON; invalid order_by is M_INVALID_PARAM
limitations: At most 1000 candidate hits per request; offset pagination

assertions: Event reports require current membership and return 404 for unknown events or non-members
Room reports need no membership and 404 for unknown rooms; user reports 404 for unknown local users
reason is required for room and user reports (M_BAD_JSON)
Reports are stored and listed for server administrators only
Only users allowed to send m.room.tombstone may upgrade (403 M_FORBIDDEN)
Unsupported versions are 400 M_UNSUPPORTED_ROOM_VERSION
The replacement has predecessor and the old room type; recommended state is copied; local and canonical aliases move
The old room receives a tombstone and events_default/invite of at least 50
limitations: Per-user settings are not transferred on join; additional_creators awaits room version 12

assertions: Depth-first walk over valid m.space.child events in spec order, cutting loops
suggested_only, max_depth, limit and from are honoured; changing walk parameters during pagination is 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
Rooms are listed only when joined/invited, joinable, knockable or world-readable; inaccessible roots are 403
Summaries include children_state with origin_server_ts, room_type, room_version and join/visibility fields
limitations: Children unknown to this server are skipped instead of fetched over federation

assertions: Non-state events from ignored users are withheld from /sync, /messages and /context
State events from ignored users are still delivered
Invites from ignored users are not delivered
Un-ignoring resumes delivery of new events
GET /devices and /devices/{id} list the caller's devices with display name and last-seen data; unknown device is 404 M_NOT_FOUND
PUT /devices/{id} renames, leaves the name unchanged when display_name is absent, and 404s for unknown devices
DELETE /devices/{id} and POST /delete_devices require UIA (m.login.password for password accounts) and succeed for already-deleted devices
Deleting a device invalidates its access tokens (hard logout), removes device keys and one-time keys, and reports the user in other users' device_lists.changed
A device recreated with a deleted device ID never accepts tokens minted for the deleted device
Re-login with a known device_id ignores initial_device_display_name and invalidates the device's previous tokens
limitations: Application-service device creation via PUT /devices (201) is not implemented: CS-API identity assertion for application services is absent server-wide

assertions: POST /logout deletes the calling device and its tokens
POST /logout/all deletes every device of the user
Requests without auth receive 401 with flows, params and session
Failed stages return 401 with errcode, the same session and completed stages
Stages outside the offered flows are refused; sessions are bound to the operation and user
Unknown sessions are an error, not a fresh challenge
Fallback pages for m.login.password and m.login.registration_token complete the stage and run the onAuthDone/postMessage script; the client then resubmits with only the session
limitations: Passwordless (identikey/SSO) accounts are offered m.login.dummy; an m.login.sso or identikey re-authentication stage is a follow-up
Sessions are process-memory only

assertions: UIA with m.login.password is required; missing new_password is M_MISSING_PARAM
logout_devices defaults to true: other devices are revoked, the requesting session survives
logout_devices false keeps every session
Without an access token the password stage identifies the user and every device is revoked
m.change_password capability is enabled only for non-guest accounts with a password
UIA is required; success returns id_server_unbind_result success (no 3PIDs to unbind)
Every token is invalidated, rooms are left (membership leave visible to others) and login returns M_USER_DEACTIVATED
erase clears profile and account data; the user ID remains unavailable
limitations: Erasure does not yet serve redacted copies of the user's events to later joiners

assertions: M_INVALID_USERNAME, M_EXCLUSIVE and M_USER_IN_USE are returned before UIA
Usernames map to lowercase localparts under the user ID grammar; numeric localparts are reserved for guests; omitted usernames are generated
inhibit_login returns only user_id; unknown kind is M_INVALID_PARAM
Application services register in their namespace with their as_token and receive M_EXCLUSIVE outside it
GET /register/available reports available, M_USER_IN_USE, M_INVALID_USERNAME, M_EXCLUSIVE and M_MISSING_PARAM
Registration tokens gate registration via m.login.registration_token and the validity endpoint; disabled registration is 403 M_FORBIDDEN on register, validity and availability
limitations: Registration tokens come from configuration and have no use limits or expiry

assertions: refresh_token true yields refresh_token and expires_in_ms; otherwise the 30-day lifetime is advertised
Expired access tokens answer M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN with soft_logout true; revoked sessions with soft_logout false
POST /refresh rotates tokens; the old refresh token stays valid until the new one is used
Unknown, revoked, logged-out and re-login-superseded refresh tokens are M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN; missing refresh_token is M_MISSING_PARAM
Soft-logout recovery by re-login with the same device keeps the device's E2EE keys
limitations: The old refresh token is revoked when the new refresh token is used, not when the new access token is first used

assertions: The deprecated access_token query parameter authenticates like the Authorization header
kind=guest is 403 M_GUEST_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN unless enabled; enabled guests get a numeric user ID and only initial_device_display_name is honoured
Guests are confined to the guest endpoint subset with M_GUEST_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN otherwise
Guests may only join rooms whose m.room.guest_access is can_join
Guests upgrade with guest_access_token and their own localpart, keeping the user ID
limitations: Guests are not removed from rooms when m.room.guest_access later stops being can_join

assertions: GET /login advertises m.login.token with get_login_token true; m.get_login_token capability is enabled for non-guests
Every call requires fresh UIA; tokens expire in 120000 ms and log in exactly once with the requested device
/.well-known/matrix/client returns m.homeserver.base_url (configured or request origin) and optional m.identity_server, with CORS
/.well-known/matrix/server returns configured delegation, else 404
/.well-known/matrix/support returns configured contacts/support page or local admins, else 404
Users may look themselves up; others need server admin, checked before lookup
Devices report sessions with connection ip, last_seen and user_agent
limitations: One session per device is reported; per-token sessions are not tracked

assertions: m.3pid_changes is disabled and GET /account/3pid is empty
add, bind and legacy add are 403 M_FORBIDDEN; delete and unbind return no-support; requestToken endpoints are 403 M_THREEPID_DENIED
limitations: No email/SMS validation or identity-server integration exists

assertions: Device keys naming another user or device are rejected with 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
Device keys must include ed25519:<device_id> and be signed by it, else 400 M_INVALID_SIGNATURE
Signed one-time and fallback keys must verify against the device key; malformed key names are M_BAD_JSON
At most one fallback key per algorithm (M_INVALID_PARAM)
A rejected upload persists nothing; an identical re-upload is not a device-list change
keys/query withholds stored device keys that are not self-signed or name another device
keys/query adds unsigned.device_display_name and merges self-signing signatures
Cross-signing keys must name the user, carry the usage, and have exactly one ed25519:<public> key
Self- and user-signing keys must be signed by the accompanying or stored master key (M_INVALID_SIGNATURE)
A cross-signing public key equal to a device ID is 403 M_FORBIDDEN 'Key ID in use'
Replacing cross-signing keys requires m.login.password UIA; exact retries and first uploads do not
keys/signatures/upload verifies each signature against the permitted signer and reports failures per user and key ID
user-signing keys and user-signing signatures are visible only to their owner
limitations: The application-service exemption from cross-signing UIA and the m.oauth stage are not implemented
Accounts without a password cannot complete replacement UIA

assertions: device_lists is only present on incremental sync
Key updates appear only for the requester and users sharing a joined room
Joining an encrypted room, or encryption being enabled, marks newly shared members changed
Users no longer sharing any encrypted room appear in left, for both the leaver and the remaining members
/keys/changes applies the same visibility between from and to; from is required (M_MISSING_PARAM) and validated (M_INVALID_PARAM)
limitations: Remote users' membership is evaluated from local room state only

assertions: Unthreaded, main-timeline and per-thread receipts coexist per (user, type, thread)
A new receipt replaces only its own scope
Sync batches one m.receipt event per room and thread scope, with thread_id on threaded receipts
thread_id must be a non-empty string naming the event's thread (main, or the thread root), else 400 M_INVALID_PARAM
Unknown receipt types are 400 M_INVALID_PARAM; a non-object body is M_BAD_JSON
Only joined members may send receipts (403 M_FORBIDDEN); the event must be in the room (404 M_NOT_FOUND)
m.read.private receipts, threaded or not, reach only their sender
limitations: m.fully_read via the receipt endpoint belongs to the read-markers handler
Receipts are not yet sent over federation as m.receipt EDUs

assertions: Only the authenticated user, joined to the room, may set typing (403 M_FORBIDDEN)
typing must be a boolean and timeout a non-negative integer (M_BAD_JSON)
Requested timeouts beyond the 30 s refresh recommendation are honoured up to a 120 s server cap
Oversized timeouts saturate without overflow or panic
Users who have left are not reported as typing
limitations: Typing is not federated as m.typing EDUs
